manifests.title: Two-stage machine
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Coupon d(p)=p-20 and tax t(q)=1.06q at p=100. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: t(d(100))=84.80, while d(t(100))=86.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Interpret f composed with g as applying g first and then f, and explain why order generally matters.

manifests.title: Order comparison
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Trace the original input through the first function, name the intermediate quantity, and feed it to the second function. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Interpret f composed with g as applying g first and then f, and explain why order generally matters.

manifests.title: Unit compatibility
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is reading f composed with g from left to right as though f acts first. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Interpret f composed with g as applying g first and then f, and explain why order generally matters.

manifests.title: Substitution slots
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: f=x^2-1,g=3x+2. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: f(g(x))=9x^2+12x+3.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Evaluate and simplify composite functions symbolically while preserving grouping and domain conditions.

manifests.title: Expression trees
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Write the substitution with parentheses before simplifying and determine both inner and outer domain conditions. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Evaluate and simplify composite functions symbolically while preserving grouping and domain conditions.

manifests.title: Outer restriction preimage
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is substituting into only one term or dropping grouping symbols. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Evaluate and simplify composite functions symbolically while preserving grouping and domain conditions.

manifests.title: Table lookup chain
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: g(2)=4 and f(4)=7. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: f(g(2))=7.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Evaluate composite functions when one or both functions are represented numerically or graphically.

manifests.title: Graph-to-graph trace
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Find the inner output, then use it as the outer input, preserving approximation when a graph is read visually. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Evaluate composite functions when one or both functions are represented numerically or graphically.

manifests.title: Undefined versus insufficient data
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is using the original input in both functions. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Evaluate composite functions when one or both functions are represented numerically or graphically.

manifests.title: Composite-domain pipeline
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: f=sqrt(u),g=x^2-9. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Domain x≤-3 or x≥3.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine the domain of a composite by enforcing both inner-function and outer-input conditions.

manifests.title: Preimage of forbidden value
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Translate outer restrictions into equations or inequalities involving the inner output, then intersect them with the inner domain. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine the domain of a composite by enforcing both inner-function and outer-input conditions.

manifests.title: Hidden restriction
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is simply intersecting the written domains of f and g as though they used the same stage variable. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine the domain of a composite by enforcing both inner-function and outer-input conditions.

manifests.title: Horizontal-line test
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Is x^2 one-to-one on all real numbers? Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: No; x and -x share outputs. Restrict to x≥0 or x≤0.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine whether a function is one-to-one and explain why one-to-one behavior is required for an inverse function.

manifests.title: Reverse mapping failure
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Check repeated outputs, use the horizontal-line test, or prove f(a)=f(b) implies a=b. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine whether a function is one-to-one and explain why one-to-one behavior is required for an inverse function.

manifests.title: Quadratic branch restrictions
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is confusing the ordinary function condition with one-to-one behavior. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine whether a function is one-to-one and explain why one-to-one behavior is required for an inverse function.

manifests.title: Coordinate reversal
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Find inverse of 3x-7. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: f^{-1}(x)=(x+7)/3.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Construct an inverse function algebraically and state the swapped domain and range.

manifests.title: Algebraic inversion
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Write y=f(x), exchange x and y, solve for y, and state the swapped domain and range. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Construct an inverse function algebraically and state the swapped domain and range.

manifests.title: Inverse versus reciprocal
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is keeping both plus and minus branches and producing an inverse relation rather than a function. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Construct an inverse function algebraically and state the swapped domain and range.

manifests.title: Inverse reflection
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Verify f=3x-2 and g=(x+2)/3. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Both compositions simplify to x.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Verify inverse functions using composition and graph symmetry across y=x.

manifests.title: Composition loop
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Compute f(f^{-1}(x)) and f^{-1}(f(x)), preserving their valid domains, and compare graph point pairs. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Verify inverse functions using composition and graph symmetry across y=x.

manifests.title: Domain-range swap
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is simplifying sqrt(x^2) to x without the branch restriction. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Verify inverse functions using composition and graph symmetry across y=x.

manifests.title: Principal root versus equation roots
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Solve sqrt(x+6)=x. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Candidates are 3 and -2; only x=3 satisfies the original equation.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Restrict power functions to one-to-one branches and connect those branches to principal radical functions.

manifests.title: Radical-exponent equivalence
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Extract perfect powers, convert between radical and rational-exponent notation, isolate a radical in an equation, raise both sides to a power, and check every candidate. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Restrict power functions to one-to-one branches and connect those branches to principal radical functions.

manifests.title: Extraneous-solution map
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is replacing sqrt(x^2) with x for negative inputs or omitting the final check. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Restrict power functions to one-to-one branches and connect those branches to principal radical functions.

manifests.title: Modeling cycle
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Costs 65,90,115,140 for 1-4 hours. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: C(h)=40+25h.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Build a multi-stage function model, state its domain and assumptions, and evaluate whether an inverse interpretation is meaningful.

manifests.title: Competing extrapolations
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Define quantities, choose a family, estimate parameters, state domain and assumptions, inspect residuals, and revise or reject when evidence disagrees. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Build a multi-stage function model, state its domain and assumptions, and evaluate whether an inverse interpretation is meaningful.

manifests.title: Residual plot
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is choosing the smoothest graph or highest fit statistic without checking meaning. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Build a multi-stage function model, state its domain and assumptions, and evaluate whether an inverse interpretation is meaningful.
